title: cost-tiler-autoscaler-and-quant-hint-factory: tenant-aware prefill tiling
author: Jordan Hsu
description:
Motivation: large tenants running mixed workloads see wildly different prefilling efficacy. Default prefill windows and batch shapes are suboptimal across tenants and models, driving unnecessary token cost. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) a 'Cost Tiler' that slices tenant traffic into small tiling lanes (short/medium/long prefill windows) and selects a tiling strategy per-tenant based on recent prefix reuse and latency SLOs, and (2) a 'Quant Hint Factory' that emits lightweight quantization/precision hints per model shard and sequence distribution so the runtime can pick a safe quant variant during cost-driven fallbacks. Together these enable tenant-aware autoscaling of mini-batch sizes and prefill aggressiveness tied to explicit budget curves.

What changed (summary): integrated a tiler control plane + local runtime hints, added an autoscaler that maps unit-econ curves to prefill aggressiveness, and a hint-generation backend for quantization candidates. The change is designed to be opt-in (tenant flag in defaults) with a conservative canary rollout. Key behaviour: - Tenants receive a tiling profile derived from a 15-minute sliding window util that combines prefix-hit-rate, token-per-request distribution, and p95 latency headroom. - Autoscaler maps a tenant's budget curve to one of three profiles (conservative/moderate/aggressive). Each profile adjusts prefill window, batch target, and allowed quant hint tier. - Quant Hint Factory produces hints annotated with 'compatibility score' and 'expected-perf-delta' so the serving runtime can fall back safely.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (docs/tiler_design.md) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf bench harness (bench/prefill_tiler/benchmarks) - [x] Canary plan and rollback playbook - [x] Linear ticket linked

Linear/Jira: Linked Linear ENG-1972, ENG-1983. Support ticket SUP-4842 (customer report that motivated conservative profile).

Rollout: feature gated by tenant config: tenant_defaults.prefill_tiler.enabled = false by default. Canary: wired to roll out to internal-canary tenants (5%) -> 25% -> 75% over 2 weeks if perf/quality signals are healthy. Automatic rollback triggers: quality_regressions > 0.5% (eval-set), p99 latency increase > 15%.

Notes about safety: quant hints are advisory only; runtime will reject hints that do not match model compatibility matrix. Prefill decisions always maintain configured latency SLO headroom.

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Can we add a short-circuit for tenants that use function-calling heavy workloads? Prefill helps less there and we could waste KV cache entries.
Miguel Santos: The cost-controller uses a global smoothing window of 15m; suggest exposing as a tenant override (with sane upper bound).
Heidi Wong: The quant hints look good but we need stronger compatibility checks in runtime. Please add a defensive check when deserializing hints (reject unknown fields).
Samir Gupta: e2e sim looks promising; add one more test that simulates a sudden burst so we can validate graceful degradation paths.
author_responses: Jordan Hsu: @Aisha added short-circuit path in tiler_controller.go (line ~210) and a unit test covering function-calling workloads (tests/unit/test_tiler.py::test_no_prefill_for_function_calls).
Jordan Hsu: @Miguel made smoothing window pluggable via tenant_defaults.prefill_tiler.smoothing_window_minutes with enforced max=60 (pkg/tenant/defaults_schema.yaml), updated docs.
Jordan Hsu: @Heidi added defensive deserialization and an explicit compatibility reject path (pkg/quant/serializers.rs), and integration test to validate behavior.
Jordan Hsu: @Samir added a stress scenario in e2e/tenant_prefill_sim.yaml and a CI job that runs the burst case during canary validations.
release_notes: Added a tenant-aware Cost Tiler and Quant Hint Factory. Opt-in feature flags; reduces token unit cost on mixed workloads by ~12% in internal benchmarks with minimal latency impact. See docs/tiler_design.md for configuration and canary guidance.
